The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

# Reform UK Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Overview
Reform UK presents a policy document outlining proposed changes across multiple sectors, with claimed potential savings of £150 billion annually and costs of £141 billion annually, plus projected growth-related tax revenues of £10 billion.

## Immigration
The party proposes freezing non-essential immigration, leaving the European Convention on Human Rights, and establishing offshore processing for asylum seekers. Foreign workers would face a 20% National Insurance rate (up from 13.8%), with exemptions for healthcare workers and small businesses. A five-year residency requirement would apply before accessing benefits. Student dependents would be barred, and foreign criminals would face immediate deportation.

## Economic Proposals
**Personal taxation:** Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000, keeping the basic rate at 20% with higher rate starting at £70,000. Stamp duty would be eliminated below £750,000. Inheritance tax would be abolished for estates under £2 million.

**Business:** Corporation tax threshold raised to £100,000 profits, with the main rate reduced from 25% to 15% over time. VAT threshold increased to £150,000. Business rates abolished for high street SMEs, offset by a 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals.

## Public Spending
Proposed 5% efficiency savings across departments (£50 billion). The Bank of England would stop paying interest on QE reserves (£35 billion). Foreign aid cut by 50% (£6 billion savings).

## NHS
Zero basic rate tax for frontline NHS staff for three years. 20% tax relief on private healthcare. Patient voucher scheme for treatment if waiting times exceed specified limits (3 days for GPs, 3 weeks for consultants, 9 weeks for operations).

## Energy
Scrap Net Zero commitments and renewable energy subsidies. Fast-track North Sea oil and gas licensing. Pursue shale gas exploration and small modular nuclear reactors.

## Policing and Justice
Recruit 40,000 new police officers over five years. Build 10,000 new detention places. Mandatory life sentences for violent repeat offenders. Reopen local magistrates' courts.

## Education
20% tax relief on independent school fees. Student loan interest scrapped. Restrict undergraduate numbers and enforce minimum entry standards.

## Defence
Increase defence spending to 3% of GDP within six years. Pay increases for armed forces personnel. Create dedicated Veterans ministry.

## Housing and Planning
Fast-track brownfield development. Abolish the Renters Reform Bill. Remove Section 24 restrictions for landlords. Prioritise local residents for social housing.

## Constitutional Changes
Leave ECHR and reform Human Rights Act. Reform House of Lords. Restrict postal voting. Hold referendum on proportional representation.

## Other Policies
- Increase farming budget to £3 billion
- End automatic EU fishing access to UK waters
- Royal Commission on social care
- Scrap HS2, ban ULEZ zones
- Reform BBC funding model

The document claims these proposals are independently costed, with detailed figures provided for each policy area.

# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Healthcare
The manifesto proposes £28bn additional annual NHS expenditure by 2030, plus £20bn capital spending over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteed rapid GP access, NHS dentistry for all (£3bn/year by 2030), boosted staff pay, restored public health budgets, and a National Cancer Plan. Mental health services would receive investment for 28-day therapy access. The party opposes NHS privatisation.

## Social Care
Proposals include free personal care (similar to Scotland's model), increased carer pay with career structures, and £20bn annual investment. Disability benefits would increase 5%, and £3bn additional funding would support children's social care.

## Housing
The party proposes 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering councils for rent controls, ending no-fault evictions, and a £29bn five-year home insulation programme. Planning reforms would protect green spaces while ensuring new developments include infrastructure.

## Energy and Climate
Proposals include wind providing 70% of electricity by 2030, no new oil/gas licences, ending fossil fuel subsidies, and community energy ownership. A carbon tax starting at £120/tonne would rise to £500/tonne within ten years. Nuclear development would cease.

## Economy and Work
The manifesto proposes £40bn average annual green investment, bringing water companies, railways, and major energy retailers into public ownership. A £15/hour minimum wage, 10:1 maximum pay ratios, repeal of anti-union legislation, and movement toward a four-day week are proposed.

## Welfare
Universal Credit would increase £40/week, the two-child benefit cap would be abolished, and the five-week benefit wait would end. Pensions would maintain inflation-linked rises, and carer's allowance would increase 10%.

## Taxation
Proposals include a 1% wealth tax on assets over £10m (2% over £1bn), aligning capital gains tax with income tax rates, and removing the upper earnings limit on National Insurance. Estimated additional revenue: £50-70bn annually by parliament's end.

## Environment and Nature
A Rights of Nature Act would give nature legal personhood. 30% of land and seas would be protected by 2030. Water companies would return to public ownership. Harmful pesticides including glyphosate would be phased out, and a new Right to Roam Act would be introduced.

## Education
School funding would increase £8bn (including £2bn teacher pay uplift). £2.5bn annually would address building safety. Tuition fees would be scrapped and maintenance grants restored. £5bn would fund SEND provision.

## Transport
Annual public transport subsidies would reach £10bn, with free bus travel for under-18s. Railways would return to public ownership. £2.5bn annually would fund cycleways and footpaths. Petrol/diesel vehicle sales would end by 2027.

## Democracy
Proposals include replacing first-past-the-post with proportional representation, votes at 16, an elected second chamber replacing the House of Lords, and repealing the Elections Act 2022.

## Immigration
The party proposes ending the hostile environment, establishing safe asylum routes, permitting asylum seekers to work during applications, and removing minimum income requirements for spousal visas.

## Foreign Policy
Commitments include an immediate Israel-Gaza ceasefire, Palestinian state recognition, ending UK arms exports to Israel, increasing overseas aid to 1% of GNI (rising to 1.5% for climate finance by 2033), and working toward EU rejoinment. The party would sign the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons and cancel Trident replacement.
